label: CKD review: Review nizatidine when the amount per dose is too high or doses are too close together for the renal regimen for the documented ulcer or reflux indication
title: Review nizatidine when the dose is too high or doses are too close together for the renal regimen
statement: For an adult outpatient with established CKD, review nizatidine when the amount per dose is too high or doses are too close together for the renal regimen for the documented ulcer or reflux indication.

plain_summary: For an adult outpatient with established CKD, review oral nizatidine when the dose is too high or doses are too close together for the recorded kidney function and treatment phase.

medicine_groups.name: Oral nizatidine
medicine_groups.note: Compare the amount per dose and the time between oral doses with the regimen for the recorded indication and treatment phase.

needs_facts.meets: Established chronic kidney disease documented by the supply date. Ask whether a clinician has told the person they have chronic kidney disease. If oral nizatidine is supplied without clinical entries and its regimen could exceed a renal limit, report only a possible finding. Ask about kidney disease, the reason for treatment and the dated creatinine clearance.

options.words: CKD was established by the supply date
CKD was absent at the supply date
CKD is known now but its timing is unclear

needs_facts.meets: Active ulcer or reflux treatment, or maintenance after healing of a duodenal ulcer. Match the documented phase to the supply directions. Ask what nizatidine treats and whether the ulcer has already healed.

options.words: Maintenance after healing of a duodenal ulcer

needs_facts.meets: Use stable creatinine clearance in mL/min applicable at supply. Check the result date against the supply date. A typed value without a verified date remains uncertain. A validated Cockcroft-Gault calculation needs contemporaneous age, sex, weight and serum creatinine with units and a recorded weight basis.

rule_for_models: For an adult outpatient with CKD established by the supply date, compare oral nizatidine strength and directions with stable creatinine clearance in mL/min at supply. At 20 to 50 inclusive, the limits are 150 mg daily for active ulcer or reflux and 150 mg every two days for maintenance after a healed duodenal ulcer. Below 20, they are 150 mg every two days and every three days respectively. Cite the supply, diagnosis, phase and dated clearance if the amount per dose is too high or doses are too close together. Report no finding for an exclusion or a regimen within every applicable limit. Otherwise report only a possible finding and name any missing fact that could change the result, including the date of an undated clearance.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish the dose taken. Kidney results obtained elsewhere, their units and their timing may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you review the nizatidine dose and the time between doses against the patient’s creatinine clearance and the reason for treatment, including whether a duodenal ulcer has healed?
